The document names a Computer Incident Response Team (CIRT) within ANTIC, Cameroon's agency, which records complaints and acts against cybercrime, and says the law requires companies to report cybercrime to ANTIC.
ANTIC says it detected and blocked 33 fraudulent loan apps, suspended 111 harassers' phone numbers and closed 4,110 of 5,533 detected fake Facebook accounts in 2025.
ANTIC states that in 2025 it recorded 17,500 complaints with total losses of 5.8 billion FCFA, and that 21,280 machines in Cameroon were in botnets.
ANTIC says its CIRT collects and analyses 200 GB of data daily to respond to nearly 200 urgent requisitions and has taken down 6,416 fake online accounts since January 2024.
ANTIC's Director General refers to the national CIRT as existing and says its application to join FIRST is ongoing.

ANTIC, Cameroon's national agency for information and communication, was restructured by Decree No 2019/150 of 22 March 2019 and runs a Computer Incident Response Team focused on cybersecurity, per the ICTAC newsletter relaying ANTIC.
CLG Global says the national cybersecurity agency ANTIC has operational responsibility for cybersecurity in Cameroon.
